correctness.rationale: For commuting idempotents h=fg=gf is idempotent and fh=gh=hf=hg=h. Its image is exactly the common fixed set and its fibers are invariant. In each fiber the common root maps to itself under both functions, each f-only or g-only fixed label maps to the root under the other function, and each remaining label independently chooses its two images from the appropriate singly fixed sets augmented by the root. Both composites then return the same root. This gives exactly the stated weighted component EGF and the labeled-set exponential formula, including the empty object. An independent finite calculation instead fixes the three fixed-label sets globally, assigns the cross-images of singly fixed labels, then counts image pairs with equal common image for every other label. Its full profile agrees with testing the original identities on all ordered pairs of functions through n=4, and it gives all eleven displayed totals through n=10. These tests supplement the bijection; they do not prove it.
residual_risks: Finite brute force in this review goes through n=4; the proof, not a census, gives all n.

value.rationale: Commuting retractions are a natural transformation-monoid object and the individual ranks and common-image rank are canonical structural invariants. The explicit component EGF recovers every labeled rank profile and gives effective exact computation without enumerating endofunction pairs; it fills a more specific gap than deciding tractability or tabulating small monoids.
residual_risks: The result does not classify all two-function logic or give unlabeled counts or asymptotics.
